paper_title: Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse
caption: Distribution of articles across political leanings of the outlets
model_annotation: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of articles across the political leanings of the media outlets, as categorized in the study "Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse." The chart is divided into four segments, each representing a different political bias category. The largest segment, colored blue, represents "Right bias" and accounts for 30.0% of the total (30 articles). The second largest, in orange, is labeled "Left bias" and constitutes 28.0% (28 articles). The green segment, labeled "Questionable source," makes up 22.0% (22 articles). The smallest segment, in red, corresponds to "Left center bias" and comprises 20.0% (20 articles). Each slice is labeled with both its percentage and the corresponding count in parentheses, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top right. The chart visually emphasizes the relative proportions of articles sourced from outlets with varying political leanings, with right-leaning outlets slightly dominating the distribution.
